Raymond III Count of Tripoli was a notable noble in the Crusader states during the twelfth century. He was born around 1140 and was the son of Raymond II Count of Tripoli and Hodierna of Jerusalem. He inherited the county after his father's death in 1152 and ruled until his own death in 1187. His reign was marked by frequent conflicts with neighboring Muslim powers and internal strife among the Frankish nobility. He sought alliances with the Kingdom of Jerusalem and the Byzantine Empire to strengthen his position. Raymond III participated in several military campaigns including the ill fated Second Crusade and later efforts to defend the northern frontier. He also played a role in the politics of the succession crisis after the death of Baldwin IV. His diplomatic maneuvers sometimes brought him into conflict with other Crusader leaders such as Guy of Lusignan. In 1187 after the disastrous Battle of Hattin Raymond III was captured by Saladin but later released under terms that required him to surrender certain fortifications. He spent his final years attempting to rebuild his shattered county before dying in 1187. His legacy is remembered for his attempts to balance independence with cooperation among the Crusader states and for his influence on the politics of the Outremer.
